questions.q: What does one value in a convolutional layer's feature map represent?
options: The learning rate used at that training step
How strongly a particular learned pattern fired at that spatial location in the input
The number of parameters in that layer
The batch index of the current example
questions.explain: Each value in a feature map indicates how strongly the corresponding learned kernel/pattern responded at that specific spatial location of the input.

questions.q: What does `nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)` do to a feature map?
options: It averages every 2x2 window and halves height and width
It keeps only the maximum value in each non-overlapping 2x2 window, halving height and width
It doubles the height and width of the feature map
It removes every other channel
questions.explain: MaxPool2d with kernel_size=2 and stride=2 slides a 2x2 window with no overlap and keeps only the maximum value in each window, halving both spatial dimensions.

questions.q: Why does max pooling give a network a small amount of tolerance to the input shifting by a pixel or two?
options: Because it increases the number of channels
Because it keeps only the strongest activation in each window and discards that activation's exact position within the window
Because it adds random noise to the input
Because it removes the need for convolution entirely
questions.explain: By keeping only the maximum value in a window and discarding its precise position, small shifts in where a pattern fires within that window don't change the pooled output.

questions.q: What makes `nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d` different from a standard `nn.AvgPool2d`?
options: It takes the max instead of the average
You specify a target output size, and it automatically determines the pooling window to reach that size regardless of the input's spatial dimensions
It cannot be used before a classifier layer
It requires a fixed batch size of 1
questions.explain: Standard pooling layers take a fixed kernel_size/stride; AdaptiveAvgPool2d instead takes a desired output_size and computes the pooling automatically to reach it, regardless of input size.

questions.q: What does `nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(output_size=(1, 1))` ('global average pooling') produce, and why is it common before a classifier head?
options: A single scalar for the entire batch, making batch size irrelevant
One value per channel, collapsing each channel's spatial map to a single number — this decouples the classifier's input size from the input image's spatial dimensions
A doubled number of channels with no spatial reduction
An error, since (1, 1) is not a valid output size
questions.explain: Global average pooling reduces each channel's entire feature map to one value, producing a fixed-size vector per sample regardless of input image size — which is why it's commonly placed right before a classifier head.
